body.en:
Almost every enquiry that starts with "China or Turkey" is really two questions bundled together: where should this item be made, and how do we get the landed cost down. They have different answers, and bundling them is why buyers change country and find the cost unchanged.

Comparing countries compares averages, and an average of a national industry says nothing about the specific supplier a buyer will deal with. The difference between a good and a poor supplier inside one country is usually larger than the difference between the two countries' averages.

Cost reduction, on the other hand, is a set of decisions about the order itself: fewer variants, simpler coatings, fuller containers, better packing, less inspection duplicated, and a schedule that lets a factory plan. Those decisions are geography-neutral, and most of them can be made with any competent supplier.

So the honest structure is: first decide whether the specification can be simplified, then decide whether the shipment can be consolidated, and only then ask which source meets the specification at the best landed cost. Buyers who start with the country usually end up optimising the smallest of the three levers.

This matters more for fasteners than for many products, because the article is cheap and heavy: the freight and the handling are a large share of the landed cost, and the material is a commodity traded on a world market. The room a country can create in the price is limited, and the room an order design can create is not.

One practical way to keep the two questions apart is to write the enquiry in two parts: a specification sheet that is identical for every source, and a cost worksheet that names the decisions the buyer controls. The specification sheet stops the country from changing the article; the worksheet stops the buyer from blaming the country for the order design.
body.zh:
"选中国还是土耳其"这类询价，其实把两个问题捆在了一起：这件东西该在哪做，以及怎样把到岸成本压下来。两个问题的答案不一样，捆在一起问，就会出现"换了国家、成本没变"的结果。

比国家，比的是平均值。一个行业的平均值，说明不了买方将要打交道的那个具体供应商。同一个国家里，好供应商和差供应商之间的差距，通常比两国平均值之间的差距更大。

而降本是关于订单本身的一组决定：减少变体、简化涂层、装满柜、改包装、不重复检验、给工厂可排产的计划。这些决定与地理无关，绝大多数在任何一家称职的供应商那里都能做。

所以诚实的问题顺序是：先看规格能不能简化，再看出货能不能合并，最后才问哪个产地能以最好的到岸成本满足这份规格。从国家入手的买方，通常在优化三个杠杆里最小的那个。

这件事对紧固件比对很多产品更要紧，因为这货便宜又重：运费和操作费占到岸成本的一大块，而材料本身是在世界市场上交易的。一个国家能在价格里腾出的空间有限，一张订单设计能腾出的空间没有上限。

heading.en: The Five Cost Blocks in a Fastener Order

heading.fr: Les cinq postes de coût d’une commande

body.en:
A fastener order's cost divides into five blocks, and each responds to a different decision. The first is material: the steel, its grade, and the scrap-to-billet market behind it. This block is set by the world market and by the specification, and it is the block a buyer influences least — except by choosing a lower grade where the design allows it.

The second is conversion: the forming, heat treatment, threading and coating. This block responds to order design more than to geography, because setup and changeover are per-variant costs. Ten variants of the same family cost more per piece than three, in any country.

The third is coating and finish, which is a specification decision rather than a price negotiation. The gap between a thin plated finish and a proper hot-dip class is a real cost difference, and it is also the difference between a part that lasts and one that does not. Cutting here is the most expensive saving available.

The fourth is packing and inspection: cartons strong enough for the route, pallets that load well, marking that traces batches, and the documents that travel with the goods. These are small per piece and large per claim when they are missing.

The fifth is freight and handling to the destination, and this is where geography actually shows up. Distance, route, transhipment, port dwell and inland leg differ by source, and for dense cargo these can outweigh any difference in unit price. A buyer comparing unit prices across sources is comparing the wrong number; the comparison belongs at landed cost.

It is worth noting which block a supplier can actually move. A supplier can improve conversion through better scheduling and can improve packing through better design; it cannot move the world steel price, and a buyer should be sceptical of any offer that appears to.
body.zh:
一张紧固件订单的成本分成五块，每块对应一个不同的决定。第一块是材料：钢材、它的牌号、以及背后的废钢—钢坯行情。这一块由世界市场和规格定，是买方影响最小的一块——除非在设计允许的地方选低一档牌号。

第二块是加工：成型、热处理、搓丝、镀层。这一块对订单设计的敏感度高于对地理的敏感度，因为换型、调机都是按变体计的成本。同一类产品做十个变体，单件成本高于只做三个，在任何国家都一样。

第三块是镀层与表面处理，这是规格决定而不是砍价决定。薄电镀和正经热镀等级之间的差价是真实的成本差，也是"能用"和"不能用"之间的差。在这里省钱，是所有省钱方式里最贵的。

第四块是包装和检验：能扛住这条航线的纸箱、装得好的托盘、能追溯批次的标记、随货的文件。单件看很小，缺了的时候，每一笔索赔都很大。

第五块是到目的地的运费和操作费，地理真正显形的地方在这里。距离、航线、中转、港口滞留、内陆段都因产地不同，而这货重，这些差别能盖过任何单价差。跨产地比单价的买方，比的是错的那个数字；比较应该落在到岸成本上。

As normas mais comuns usadas no comércio internacional de fixadores são ISO 898-1 (propriedades mecânicas), ISO 3506-1 (aço inoxidável), ISO 3269 (inspeção de aceitação), ISO 4042 (revestimentos) e ISO 1502 (calibres de rosca). body.en:
The two sources are different industries with different strengths, not two prices for the same thing. China's fastener industry is large, deep in range, and organised around volume production: a buyer can find almost any standard item, in almost any coating, from a supplier base that competes on scale. That depth is the advantage — the range and the tooling exist, and lead times for standard items are short.

Turkey's fastener industry is smaller and closer to European and Middle Eastern markets, with a shorter sea route to the Mediterranean, the Black Sea and parts of Africa, and a trading culture built around those routes. Its advantage is proximity and responsiveness: shorter transit, smaller minimums, and a supply relationship that can flex.

Where the two overlap is in the middle of the range: standard bolts, nuts and screws in common grades with common coatings. There, the choice usually comes down to freight and to the buyer's own logistics, not to the factory.

Where they do not overlap is at the edges. A specialty coating, an unusual dimension, a proprietary item or a large-volume standard programme is usually a China question, because the tooling and the capacity are there. A small order needed quickly, or one that has to arrive through a Mediterranean port, is often a Turkey question, because the route is shorter and the minimums are lower.

The error to avoid is treating one source as a benchmark for the other. A buyer who negotiates a China price and asks a Turkish supplier to match it is asking a smaller industry to behave like a larger one; the answer will be either a refusal or a quiet change in what is being supplied.

A third consideration is the language of the paperwork. Both industries work in English for export, and the difference is in the detail: which standards are cited by default, which inspection conventions are assumed, and how quickly a technical question is answered. That is a relationship cost, and it is usually discovered after the first order rather than before it.
body.zh:
这两个产地是两个不同的行业、各有各的长处，不是同一件东西的两个价格。中国紧固件行业规模大、品类深、围绕批量生产组织起来：买方几乎能找到任何一种标准件、任何一种涂层，供应基础靠规模竞争。深度就是优势——品类和工装都在，标准件的交期短。

土耳其紧固件行业规模小一些，离欧洲和中东市场更近，到地中海、黑海和部分非洲的海运航程更短，贸易文化也是围着这些航线长出来的。它的优势是近和快：在途短、起订量低、供应关系可以商量。

两者重叠的地方在品类中段：常见等级、常见涂层的标准螺栓、螺母、螺钉。这一段的选择，通常由运费和买方自己的物流决定，而不是由工厂决定。

不重叠的地方在两端。特殊涂层、非常规尺寸、专有件、大批量标准项目，通常是中国的问题，因为工装和产能都在那边。急着要的小单，或者必须从地中海港口进的货，往往是土耳其的问题，因为航线短、起订量低。

要避免的错误，是拿一个产地当另一个的基准。用中国的价格去要求土耳其供应商对标，等于让一个较小的行业表现得像一个较大的行业；答案要么是拒绝，要么是悄悄换掉供给的东西。

heading.fr: Où se trouvent réellement les économies
heading.ja: 削減分は実際どこにあるのか

body.en:
The savings that actually materialise are the boring ones, and they are available regardless of source. The largest is specification discipline: cutting the number of coatings, sizes and packing variants in an order reduces conversion cost more than any negotiation, and it reduces the risk of a mixed delivery.

The second is consolidation: combining several items into one shipment so that the container fills on weight rather than on air. For dense cargo, this is usually the single biggest lever after the specification, because it attacks the freight block directly.

The third is documentation done once: a specification, a packing standard, an inspection plan and a document set agreed at the start, and reused for every repeat order. Each renegotiation of these costs management time on both sides, and it is time that shows up as a higher price rather than as an invoice.

The fourth is stock policy: buying to a schedule rather than to an emergency reduces both the unit price and the freight per piece, because planned orders can be consolidated and urgent ones cannot. Emergency buying is expensive in every country.

What does not produce savings is switching country to chase a headline price. The headline price is the smallest block, and a switch resets the relationship, the documentation and the inspection history — all of which have a cost that the first invoice does not show.

It is also worth measuring the savings rather than assuming them. A buyer who tracks landed cost per piece across several orders can see whether the specification discipline and the consolidation actually moved the number, and can stop paying attention to the levers that did not.
body.zh:
真正能落地的节省都是些乏味的动作，而且与产地无关。最大的一项是规格纪律：减少订单里的涂层种类、尺寸种类、包装变体，降本效果超过任何谈判，同时还降低了混装风险。

第二项是合并：把几个品项并成一票，让集装箱按重量装满，而不是装了一半空气。对重货来说，这通常是规格之后最大的杠杆，因为它直接打在运费那块上。

第三项是一次性把文件做完：规格、包装标准、检验方案、文件清单，开工时定好，之后每张返单沿用。每重谈一次，双方都花管理时间，而这些时间最后是以更高价格的形式出现，而不是以发票的形式。

第四项是库存策略：按计划买而不是按救火买，单价和单件运费都会下来，因为计划单能合并、急单不能。急单在哪个国家都贵。

不产生节省的，是为了一个头条价格换产地。头条价格是最小的那一块，而换产地会重置关系、文件和检验历史——这些都有成本，只是第一张发票上看不出来。

body.en:
Before switching source, four things should be verified, and they are all about the same article rather than about the country. The first is specification equivalence: the same grade, the same coating class, the same tolerances, the same marking. A cheaper offer that is not the same article is not a cheaper offer.

The second is the sample and the batch evidence: a sample that can be measured against the drawing, and a batch record that shows the sample came from a production run rather than from a bench. In both countries, a good sample proves the capability and says nothing about the routine.

The third is the packing and the route: what the cartons are, how they stack, which port, which inland leg, and how long the whole journey takes. A shorter sea route with a slower inland leg is not a shorter journey.

The fourth is the paperwork the destination requires: the documents that must travel with the goods, the certification that must be arranged per order, and the marking the customs and the customer expect. These are the same requirements whichever source is used, and a new source has to be brought up to them rather than assumed to know them.

Once those four are established, the comparison is a landed cost comparison, and it will sometimes say that the incumbent is cheaper. That is a useful answer: the exercise has priced the switch, and the price was higher than the difference.

One last check is the second order. A source that delivered a good first shipment and a different second one has told you what its routine is, and the routine is what a buyer actually buys.
body.zh:
换产地之前要核实四件事，而且都关于同一件东西，不关于国家。第一是规格等效：同样的牌号、同样的镀层等级、同样的公差、同样的标记。更便宜的报价如果不是同一件东西，那就不是更便宜的报价。

第二是样品与批次证据：一个能对着图纸量的样品，加上一份能说明这样品来自生产批次、不是台面上做出来的批次记录。在两个国家，好样品都只证明能力，不证明日常。

第三是包装和航线：箱子是什么、怎么码、走哪个港、内陆段怎么走、整段要多久。海运短但内陆慢，不等于整段短。

第四是目的地要求的单证：必须随货走的文件、要按订单去办的认证、海关和客户要看的标记。这些要求用哪个产地都一样，新产地要被带到这个水平上，而不是假定它已经知道。

这四样确认完，比较才是到岸成本比较；而它有时会告诉你现任更便宜。这个结论有用：这次演练给"换"定了价，而定价高于差价。

body.en:
Buyers comparing sources ask a handful of questions, and the useful answers are usually about what is being compared.

The most common is which country is cheaper. The honest answer is that the averages differ by less than the spread inside each country, so the question is which supplier, not which country. The second is whether a cheaper quote means a lower grade; sometimes it does, and the way to find out is to compare the specification line by line rather than the price line.

The third is whether one source can serve a whole range. China usually can, in volume; Turkey usually can, in a narrower range and with more flexibility on minimums. The fourth is whether a switch is worth the disruption; it is worth it when the specification cannot be met by the incumbent, and it is rarely worth it for a headline price.

See frequently asked questions below.
